To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain network architecture of the human brain is scale free.

1) the human brain is organized in a complex network of functional connections, which are highly dynamic, 2) these connections are organized in a small world architecture, and 3) the small world architecture is the result of a balance between local and long-range connectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the brain as a complex network of interacting components.
the development and application of network science [2,3].
understanding how the human brain works, and how we can leverage that understanding to develop new technologies for brain health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is the most complex organ in the human body.
the brain is a network of networks and that the brain is not only composed of neurons but also of glial cells.
the brain is an extremely complex and dynamic organ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to use network science to understand the organization of the brain.
the brain is a complex network of networks, and that network science provides an ideal language to describe the brain.
we have developed a new approach to studying the brain and its dynamics, which we call the "network approach."
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can understand the structure of the brain in terms of the structure of the connectome.
we can use network science to understand the human brain.
the human brain is not a collection of independent parts.
